text: One of the most overlooked advantages in stock investing is learning from someone who has already navigated the market’s ups and downs. Stocks aren’t just about picking winners, understanding valuation, managing risk, and avoiding emotional decisions matters just as much. The right mentor can help you learn faster, avoid costly mistakes, and build confidence in your decisions. Sometimes, the best investment you can make is in your own knowledge.

I disagree to an extent. Some advisors are just good at marketing themselves. I’ve seen people pay for expensive courses and still lose money. Personally, I believe independent research and learning to question everything are just as important.

I think all the points are valid. Mentorship isn't a guarantee of profits, and experience alone doesn't make someone a good teacher. The key is finding someone transparent about risk, willing to explain their reasoning, and honest about mistakes. Combine that guidance with your own research, and you're building a much stronger foundation.
